full/full: The training loss is an average over all N examples, so its gradient is the average of N per-example gradients.
full/cost: With fifty thousand images, one exact step would take fifty thousand forward and backward passes.
full/batch: So draw a small random batch of B examples, and average only theirs. It estimates the same gradient, at a fraction of the cost.
average/per: Say B is four, and for one weight the four examples give gradients of two, minus one, three and zero.
average/mean: The minibatch gradient is their mean: they add up to four, and four over four is one.
average/noise: Another batch gives another estimate. Batch after batch, they scatter around the true gradient.
average/size: Bigger batches scatter less, but each step costs more. Small batches buy many cheap, noisy steps.
epoch/epoch: One pass through all N examples is called an epoch.
epoch/count: Each step uses one batch of B, so an epoch takes N over B steps. Twelve hundred examples in batches of a hundred: twelve steps.
epoch/seen: And after k steps, the model has seen k times B examples. Five steps of a hundred: five hundred.
example/ask: Your turn to follow along. A training set has fifty thousand examples, and the batch size is a hundred. How many steps make one epoch?
example/divide: Each step uses a hundred examples, so divide: fifty thousand over a hundred.
